source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτά φησιν ὁ παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαῖος ὅτι πολλὰ ἔχων λέγειν περὶ τῶν κατὰ τὸν Ἰησοῦν γενομένων καὶ ἀληθῆ καὶ οὐ παραπλήσια τοῖς ὑπὸ τῶν μαθητῶν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ γραφεῖσιν ἑκὼν ἐκεῖνα παραλείπω. τίνα οὖν ἄρα τἀληθῆ καὶ οὐχ ὁποῖα ἐν τοῖς εὐαγγελίοις γέγραπται, ἃ παραλείπει ὁ παρὰ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαῖος; ἢ δοκούσῃ δεινότητι ῥητορικῇ χρησάμενος προσποιεῖται μὲν ἔχειν λέγειν οὐδὲν δὲ εἶχεν ἔξωθεν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου φέρειν, δυνάμενον πλῆξαι ὡς ἀληθὲς τὸν ἀκούοντα καὶ ὡς ἐναργῶς κατηγοροῦν Ἰησοῦ καὶ τῆς διδασκαλίας αὐτοῦ; ἐγκαλεῖ δὲ τοῖς μαθηταῖς ὡς πλασαμένοις ὅτι πάντα τὰ συμβάντα αὐτῷ ἐκεῖνος προῄδει καὶ προειρήκει. καὶ τοῦτο δὲ ἀληθὲς ὂν, κἂν μὴ Κέλσος βούληται, παραστήσομεν ἀπὸ πολλῶν καὶ ἄλλων προφητικῶς ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος εἰρημένων, ἐν οἷς προεῖπε τὰ Χριστιανοῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ὕστερον γενόμενα γενεαῖς. καὶ τίς γε οὐκ ἂν θαυμάσαι τὸ προειρημένον τὸ „ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας δὲ καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ, εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσι,“ καὶ εἴ τι ἄλλο περὶ τοῦ διωχθήσεσθαι τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ προεῖπε. διὰ ποῖον γὰρ δόγμα τῶν ἐν ἀνθρώποις γεγενημένων κολάζονται καὶ ἄλλοι, ἵνα τις τῶν κατηγορούντων Ἰησοῦ λέγῃ ὅτι ὁρῶν τὰ ἀσεβῆ ἢ τὰ ψευδῆ τῶν δογμάτων κατηγορούμενα ἔδοξε καὶ τοῦτο σεμνύνειν διὰ τοῦ προλέγειν δῆθεν περὶ αὐτοῦ; εἴπερ γὰρ ἐχρῆν διὰ δόγματα „ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας καὶ βασιλεῖς“ ἄγεσθαί τινας, καὶ τίνας ἐχρῆν ἄλλους ἢ Ἐπικουρείους, τοὺς πάντῃ πρόνοιαν ἀναιροῦντας, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ Περιπάτου, μηδὲν φάσκοντας ἀνύειν εὐχὰς καὶ τὰς ὡς πρὸς τὸ θεῖον θυσίας; ἀλλὰ φήσει τις ὅτι καὶ Σαμαρεῖς διὰ τὴν ἑαυτῶν θεοσέβειαν διώκονται. πρὸς ὃν τοιαῦτα ἐροῦμεν· οἱ Σικάριοι διὰ τὴν περιτομὴν ὡς ἀκρωτηριάζοντες παρὰ τοὺς καθεστῶτας νόμους καὶ τὰ Ἰουδαίοις συγκεχωρημένα μόνοις ἀναιροῦνται. καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἀκοῦσαι δικαστοῦ πυνθανομένου, εἰ κατὰ τήνδε τὴν νομιζομένην θεοσέβειαν ὁ Σικάριος ἀγωνιζόμενος βιοῦν μεταθέμενος μὲν ἀπολυθήσεται ἐμμένων δὲ τὴν ἐπὶ θανάτῳ ἀπαχθήσεται· ἀλλὰ γὰρ ἀρκεῖ δειχθεῖσα ἡ περιτομὴ πρὸς ἀναίρεσιν τοῦ πεπονθότος αὐτήν. Χριστιανοὶ δὲ μόνοι κατὰ τὰ εἰρημένα ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος αὐτῶν λέγοντος· „ἐπὶ ἡγεμόνας καὶ βασιλεῖς ἀχθήσεσθε ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ“ μέχρι τελευταίας ἀναπνοῆς ὑπὸ τῶν δικαστῶν ἐπιτρέπονται ἐξομοσάμενοι τὸν χριστιανισμὸν καὶ κατὰ τὰ κοινὰ ἔθη θύσαντες καὶ ὀμόσαντες οἴκοι γενέσθαι καὶ ζῆν ἀκινδύνως. ὅρα δὲ εἰ μὴ μετὰ πολλῆς ἐξουσίας λέγεται τὸ „πᾶς ὃς ἐὰν ὁμολογήσῃ ἐν ἐμοὶ ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων, κἀγὼ ὁμολογήσω ἐν αὐτῷ ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ πατρός μου τοῦ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· καὶ πᾶς ὃς ἐὰν ἀρνήσηταί με ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων,“ καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς. καὶ ἀνάβα μοι τῷ λόγῳ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν λέγοντα ταῦτα, καὶ ὅρα μηδέπω γενόμενα προφητευόμενα εἰ μὴ φήσεις ἀπιστῶν μὲν αὐτῷ ὅτι ταῦτα φλυαρεῖ καὶ μάτην λέγει (οὐ γὰρ ἔσται τὰ λεγόμενα), ἀμφιβάλλων δὲ περὶ τοῦ συγκαταθέσθαι τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ εἰ μὴ ὅτι, ἐὰν ταῦτα πληρωθῇ καὶ συστῇ ἡ διδασκαλία τῶν λόγων τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὡς φροντίζειν τοὺς ἡγεμόνας καὶ τοὺς βασιλεῖς ἀναιρεῖν τοὺς ὁμολογοῦντας τὸν Ἰησοῦν, τότε πιστεύσομεν ὅτι ὡς μεγάλην ἐξουσίαν λαβὼν ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ πρὸς τὸ σπεῖραι τοῦτον τὸν λόγον τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ πειθόμενος κρατήσειν αὐτὸν ταῦτά φησι. τίς δ᾿ οὐ θαυμάσεται ἀναβαίνων τῷ λόγῳ ἐπ᾿ ἐκεῖνον διδάσκοντα τότε καὶ λέγοντα· „κηρυχθήσεται τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦτο ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσι“ καὶ θεωρῶν κατὰ τὰ ὑπ᾿ ἐκείνου εἰρημένα κεκηρυγμένον τὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εὐαγγέλιον ἐν τῇ ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν „Ἕλλησι καὶ βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς καὶ ἀνοήτοις“; πᾶσαν γὰρ φύσιν ἀνθρώπων ὁ μετὰ δυνάμεως λαληθεὶς λόγος κεκράτηκε· καὶ οὐκ ἔστι τι γένος ἰδεῖν ἀνθρώπων, ὃ ἐκπέφευγε παραδέξασθαι τὴν Ἰησοῦ διδασκαλίαν. ὁ δὲ ἀπιστῶν παρὰ τῷ Κέλσῳ Ἰουδαῖος περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὅτι πάντα τὰ συμβάντα αὐτῷ προῄδει, κατανοησάτω, τίνα τρόπον ἔτι συνεστώσης τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαϊκῆς λατρείας γινομένης ἐν αὐτῇ προεῖπεν Ἰησοῦς τὰ συμβησόμενα αὐτῇ ὑπὸ Ῥωμαίων. οὐ γὰρ δὴ τοὺς αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ γνωρίμους καὶ ἀκροατὰς φήσουσι χωρὶς γραφῆς τὴν τῶν εὐαγγελίων παραδεδωκέναι διδασκαλίαν καὶ καταλιπεῖν τοὺς μαθητὰς χωρὶς τῶν περὶ Ἰησοῦ ἐν γράμμασιν ὑπομνημάτων. γέγραπται δὴ ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸ „ὅταν δὲ ἴδητε κυκλουμένην ὑπὸ στρατοπέδων τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ, τότε γνῶτε ὅτι ἤγγισεν ἡ ἐρήμωσις αὐτῆς.“ καὶ οὐδαμῶς τότε ἦν στρατόπεδα περὶ τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ κυκλοῦντα αὐτὴν καὶ περιέχοντα καὶ πολιορκοῦντα. τοῦτο γὰρ ἤρξατο μὲν ἔτι Νέρωνος βασιλεύοντος παρέτεινε δὲ ἕως τῆς Οὐεσπασιανοῦ ἡγεμονίας· οὗ ὁ υἱὸς Τίτος καθεῖλε τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ, ὡς μὲν Ἰώσηπος γράφει, διὰ Ἰάκωβον τὸν δίκαιον, τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰησοῦ τοῦ λεγομένου Χριστοῦ, ὡς δὲ ἡ ἀλήθεια παρίστησι, διὰ Ἰησοῦν τὸν Χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: After these things says (φημί) the Jew in Celsus that 'having much to say (ἔχων λέγειν) about the things that happened concerning Jesus, both true (ἀληθῆ) and not resembling (οὐ παραπλήσια) the things written (γράφω) by the disciples (μαθηταί) of Jesus, willingly (ἑκών) I pass those over (παραλείπω).' What then are the true things, not such as are written in the gospels (εὐαγγέλια), which the Jew in Celsus passes over? Or, using a seeming (δοκούσῃ) rhetorical cleverness (δεινότης ῥητορική), does he pretend (προσποιέομαι) to have [something] to say, but had nothing to bring from outside (ἔξωθεν) the gospel able to strike (πλήσσω) the hearer as true and as clearly (ἐναργῶς) accusing (κατηγορέω) Jesus and his teaching (διδασκαλία)? He charges (ἐγκαλέω) the disciples as having fabricated (πλάσσομαι) that he foreknew (προοίδα) and had foretold (προεῖπον) all the things that befell (συμβαίνω) him. This, being true even if Celsus does not wish, we shall establish (παρίστημι) from many other things said prophetically (προφητικῶς) by the Saviour (σωτήρ), in which he foretold the things [that would befall] Christians even in later generations (γενεαί). Who would not marvel at the foretold '[before] governors (ἡγεμόνας) and kings you will be led (ἄγω, fut. pass.) for my sake, for a testimony (μαρτύριον) to them and to the nations (ἔθνη)', and whatever else he foretold about his disciples being persecuted (διώκω)? For on account of what doctrine (δόγμα) of those that have arisen among men are others also punished (κολάζω), so that one of the accusers of Jesus might say that, seeing the impious (ἀσεβῆ) or false of doctrines accused, he thought (δοκέω) to dignify (σεμνύνω) this too by supposedly (δῆθεν) foretelling about it? For if it were necessary (χρή) for some to be led 'before governors and kings' because of doctrines, whom else ought it to be than Epicureans, who abolish (ἀναιρέω) providence (πρόνοια) entirely, and also those from the Peripatos, saying prayers (εὐχαί) and sacrifices (θυσίαι) as to the divine (τὸ θεῖον) accomplish (ἀνύω) nothing? But someone will say that Samaritans too are persecuted for their own religion (θεοσέβεια). To him we shall say such things: the Sicarii (Σικάριοι) on account of circumcision (περιτομή), as mutilating (ἀκρωτηριάζω) against the established laws and the things conceded (συγχωρέω) to Jews alone, are put to death (ἀναιρέω). And it is not possible to hear a judge (δικαστής) inquiring whether the Sicarius, striving to live by this reputed (νομιζομένη) religion, if he changes (μετατίθεμαι) will be released (ἀπολύω), but if he remains (ἐμμένω) will be led away to death; but circumcision, shown (δείκνυμι), suffices for the killing of the one who underwent it. But Christians alone, according to what was said by their Saviour saying 'before governors and kings you will be led for my sake', until their last breath (ἀναπνοή) are permitted (ἐπιτρέπω) by the judges, having forsworn (ἐξόμνυμι) Christianity (χριστιανισμός) and having sacrificed (θύω) according to common customs (ἔθη) and having sworn (ὄμνυμι), to go home and live without danger (ἀκινδύνως). See whether not with much authority (ἐξουσία) is said the 'everyone who confesses (ὁμολογέω) in me before men, I too will confess in him before my Father (πατήρ) in the heavens; and everyone who denies (ἀρνέομαι) me before men', and the following. And go up (ἀνάβηθι) for me in thought (λόγῳ) to Jesus saying these things, and see things prophesied (προφητεύω) not yet having happened, whether you will not say, disbelieving (ἀπιστέω) him, that he babbles (φλυαρέω) these things and speaks in vain (μάτην) (for the things said will not be), but, doubting (ἀμφιβάλλω) about assenting (συγκατατίθεμαι) to his words, [will you not say] that if these things are fulfilled (πληρόω) and the teaching of Jesus' words is established (συνίσταμαι), so that governors and kings take care (φροντίζω) to kill those confessing Jesus, then we shall believe that as having received great authority from God (θεός) to sow (σπείρω) this word (λόγος) to the race (γένος) of men and being persuaded (πείθομαι) that he will prevail (κρατέω) he says these things? Who will not marvel, going up in thought to him teaching then and saying 'this gospel will be preached (κηρύσσω) in the whole world (κόσμος) for a testimony to them and to the nations', and beholding (θεωρέω), according to what was said by him, the gospel of Jesus Christ (Χριστός) preached in the [land] under heaven 'to Greeks and barbarians, wise and foolish (ἀνόητοι)'? For the word spoken with power (δύναμις) has mastered every nature (φύσις) of men; and there is no race of men to see which has escaped (ἐκφεύγω) receiving (παραδέχομαι) the teaching of Jesus. Let the Jew in Celsus, disbelieving about Jesus that he foreknew all the things that befell him, consider (κατανοέω) in what manner, Jerusalem still standing (συνίσταμαι) and all the Jewish worship (λατρεία) being performed in it, Jesus foretold the things that would befall it by Romans. For they will not say that the very acquaintances (γνώριμοι) and hearers (ἀκροαταί) of Jesus handed down (παραδίδωμι) without writing (γραφή) the teaching of the gospels and left (καταλείπω) the disciples without written memoirs (ὑπομνήματα) about Jesus. It is written in them: 'when you see Jerusalem being surrounded (κυκλόω) by armies (στρατόπεδα), then know that its desolation (ἐρήμωσις) has drawn near (ἐγγίζω).' And by no means were there then armies around Jerusalem encircling and enclosing (περιέχω) and besieging (πολιορκέω) it. For this began while Nero was still reigning (βασιλεύω) and extended (παρατείνω) until the rule (ἡγεμονία) of Vespasian; whose son Titus destroyed (καθαιρέω) Jerusalem, as Josephus writes, on account of James the Just (δίκαιος), the brother of Jesus called (λεγόμενος) Christ, but as the truth (ἀλήθεια) shows, on account of Jesus the Christ of God.
pass_b_english: After this Celsus’s Jew says: “Though I have much to say about what happened in Jesus’ life, things that are true and unlike what Jesus’ disciples wrote, I deliberately pass them over.” What, then, are these true things, unlike what is written in the Gospels, that Celsus’s Jew passes over? Or is he using what passes for rhetorical skill, pretending that he has something to say, when in fact he had nothing from outside the Gospel to bring forward that could strike the hearer as true and as a clear accusation against Jesus and his teaching?

He charges the disciples with having invented the claim that Jesus foreknew and foretold everything that happened to him. That this too is true, whether Celsus likes it or not, we shall show from many other things the Saviour spoke prophetically, in which he foretold what would happen to Christians even in later generations. Who would not marvel at the prediction, “You will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the nations” (Matthew 10:18), and at whatever else he foretold about the persecution of his disciples? For on account of what doctrine, among all that have arisen among men, are others punished too, so that one of Jesus’ accusers could say that Jesus, seeing impious or false doctrines being prosecuted, thought he would lend dignity to this one too by an alleged prediction about it? If anyone had to be brought “before governors and kings” (Matthew 10:18) for their doctrines, who should it have been but the Epicureans, who do away with providence altogether, and the Peripatetics as well, who say that prayers and the sacrifices offered as to the divine achieve nothing?

But someone will say that the Samaritans too are persecuted for their religion. To him we shall reply: the Sicarii are put to death because of circumcision, as men who mutilate the body contrary to the established laws and to what is granted to the Jews alone. And you will not hear a judge asking whether a Sicarius who strives to live by this supposed religion will be released if he changes his mind, but led off to death if he holds firm. No, proof of circumcision is enough to have the man who underwent it put to death. Christians alone, in keeping with what their Saviour said, “You will be brought before governors and kings for my sake” (Matthew 10:18), are allowed by the judges, right up to their last breath, once they have forsworn Christianity, sacrificed according to the common customs and taken the oath, to go home and live without danger.

See whether it is not with great authority that these words are spoken: “Everyone who acknowledges me before men, I also will acknowledge before my Father who is in heaven; and everyone who denies me before men,” and the rest (Matthew 10:32–33). Go back with me in thought to Jesus as he says these things, and look at things prophesied that had not yet happened. See whether you would not say, if you disbelieved him, that he was talking nonsense and speaking in vain, since what he said would not come to pass; or, if you were in two minds about assenting to his words, whether you would not say: “If these things are fulfilled, and the teaching of Jesus’ words becomes established, so that governors and kings take pains to put to death those who acknowledge Jesus, then we shall believe that he says these things as one who has received great authority from God to sow this word in the human race, and who is convinced that it will prevail.”

Who will not marvel, going back in thought to him as he then taught and said, “This gospel will be preached in the whole world, as a testimony to them and to the nations” (Matthew 24:14), and seeing that, just as he said, the gospel of Jesus Christ has been preached throughout the world under heaven “to Greeks and barbarians, to wise and foolish” (Romans 1:14)? For the word spoken with power has prevailed over every kind of human nature, and no race of men can be found that has escaped receiving the teaching of Jesus.

Let Celsus’s Jew, who does not believe that Jesus foreknew all that happened to him, consider how, while Jerusalem still stood and the whole Jewish worship was carried on in it, Jesus foretold what would befall it at the hands of the Romans. For surely they will not say that Jesus’ own acquaintances and hearers handed down the teaching of the Gospels without writing and left their disciples without written records about Jesus. Now it is written in them: “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near” (Luke 21:20). At that time there were no armies at all around Jerusalem, encircling it, enclosing it and besieging it. That began while Nero was still emperor and went on until the reign of Vespasian, whose son Titus destroyed Jerusalem: as Josephus writes, on account of James the Just, the brother of Jesus who was called Christ; but as the truth shows, on account of Jesus the Christ of God.

choices.why: οὐ παραπλήσια: 'not at all like' -> 'unlike' (removed added intensifier); ἑκών: 'willingly' -> 'deliberately'

ὁρῶν ... ἔδοξε: made clear the accuser says Jesus saw the doctrines prosecuted (English 'he saw' could be read as the accuser); δῆθεν προλέγειν: 'pretending to foretell its fate' -> 'an alleged prediction about it' (removed added 'fate')
κολάζονται καὶ ἄλλοι: 'are any others punished' -> 'are others punished too'
ἐξομοσάμενοι ... θύσαντες ... ὀμόσαντες οἴκοι γενέσθαι: permission now attaches to going home after forswearing, sacrificing and swearing, as the participles frame it
μηδέπω γενόμενα προφητευόμενα: 'what was prophesied before it had yet happened' -> 'things prophesied that had not yet happened'; οὐ γὰρ ἔσται: 'would never' -> 'would not' (removed added 'never')
κεκράτηκε: 'mastered' -> 'prevailed over', matching κρατήσειν earlier in the chapter
translator note corrected: Matthew 10:18 itself has δέ, so Origen's first form keeps it rather than adding it
Scripture checked: Matthew 10:18, 10:32-33, 24:14 (merged saying, note kept), Romans 1:14, Luke 21:20 all match the quoted words

Scripture citations sit inline beside the clause in Pass B.

translator_notes: The Jew’s opening statement is in the first person (παραλείπω), so it is quoted directly. The disciples’ ‘invention’ charge is reported indirectly and is left unquoted. Matthew 10:18 is quoted three times; Origen’s first form keeps Matthew’s δέ (dropping the opening καί) and reads τοῖς ἔθνεσι; the later two forms drop δέ, one stopping before the verb and one at ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ (‘nations’ kept for ἔθνη; ‘Gentiles’ is equally possible). Matthew 10:32-33: ‘acknowledge’ for ὁμολογέω ἐν (a Semitic construction, ‘confess in’); Origen cuts the quotation off with καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς, which the English keeps as ‘and the rest’. The ‘preached in the whole world’ saying merges Matthew 24:14 (κηρυχθήσεται τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ... ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ οἰκουμένῃ εἰς μαρτύριον πᾶσι τοῖς ἔθνεσιν) with the wording of Matthew 26:13 / Mark 14:9 (ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ) and Matthew 10:18 (εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν); cited as Matthew 24:14, the closest whole saying. ‘Sow this word’ may echo the parable of the sower (Matthew 13:3-23), but that is uncertain and not cited inline. ‘Sicarii’: Origen uses the name for a group (apparently Samaritan) put to death for circumcision under the imperial ban, which exempted Jews; the English keeps his term. The passage in which Josephus says Jerusalem fell because of James is not in the surviving text of Josephus (Origen reports it again in Contra Celsum 1.47); ‘Jesus who was called Christ’ is Josephus’s phrase (compare Antiquities 20.200), not a Gospel citation. ‘The Christ of God’ is a title (compare Luke 9:20) and is not given an inline citation. The long sentence beginning ‘See whether you would not say’ is one Greek period with two branches (ἀπιστῶν μέν ... ἀμφιβάλλων δέ ... εἰ μὴ ὅτι); the English keeps both branches as one sentence and quotes the doubter’s imagined words.
